query: "Kapitän zur See" Ernst Lindemann was the commander of which one of two battleships built for Nazi Germany's "Kriegsmarine"?

pipeline_result.response:
The battleship "Bismarck". 

This can be deduced from the context provided, where it is mentioned that Ernst Heinrich Lindemann was the commander of the battleship "Bismarck", which was a key component in the German naval fleet during World War II. The passage specifically states: "Ernst Heinrich Lindemann (25 January 1833 in Kirchlengern – 8 May 1900 in Düsseldorf) was German politician and mayor of Essen, Dortmund and Düsseldorf. His grandson 'Kapitän zur See' Ernst Lindemann was the commander of the battleship 'Bismarck'."
retrieved_context: Ernst Lindemann: Otto Ernst Lindemann (28 March 1894 – 27 May 1941) was a German "Kapitän zur See" (naval captain).  He was the only commander of the battleship "Bismarck" during its eight months of service in World War II.

Ernst Heinrich Lindemann: Ernst Heinrich Lindemann (25 January 1833 in Kirchlengern – 8 May 1900 in Düsseldorf) was German politician and mayor of Essen, Dortmund and Düsseldorf.  His grandson "Kapitän zur See" Ernst Lindemann was the commander of the battleship "Bismarck".

Hansjürgen Reinicke: Hans-Jürgen "Hansjürgen" Rudolf Reinicke (10 August 1902 – 29 January 1978) was a "Kapitän zur See", commander of heavy cruiser "Prinz Eugen", in Nazi Germany's "Kriegsmarine" during the Second World War and recipient of the Knight's Cross of the Iron Cross.
